<description>
Based on:
- #36716

`poll()` reports an error or hangup on a socket whether or not we asked for it. If that happens for a peer we did not request to read from, disconnect directly. This just adds clarity: previously we would attempt a send that would then fail. The only side-effect is a changed log message. Nothing changes with `select()`: since #36716 it no longer reports errors for established connections.

The last commit does the same for HTTP, where on error it also no longer attempts a final read from a client whose reads are paused.

As a followup to #36716, `p2p_socket_errors.py` adds coverage for existing behavior:
- the node ignores a single urgent byte: the connection stays open, ordinary data is still processed and the urgent byte is not counted as received.
- a peer reset while the node is sending (the change above only changes the log message)

Similarly `interface_http.py` checks that:
- a single urgent byte does not disturb an ordinary request.
- a client reset while the server has unsent responses (the HTTP change only changes the log message)

Two commits only move code:
- the send-stall wait moves from `p2p_ping_ibd.py` into the test framework, so the new tests can use it.
- the `wait_ignores_urgent_data` unit test from #36716 moves next to the other wait test. It was placed above the socket pair tests there to ease backporting.
</description>

<commits>
d87ab6523d net: only use the select error set while connecting

Windows uses the select() error set to report a failed non-blocking
connect(). Make ErrorEvent an event that can be requested from
Sock::Wait(), like RecvEvent and SendEvent: with select() it adds the
socket to the error set. ConnectToSocket() requests it while
connecting. This is safe on all platforms, as any error condition is
worth waking for there.

All other uses of select() now leave the error set empty. With
select(), sockets waited on without ErrorEvent no longer wake up for
or report exceptional conditions, such as TCP urgent data on an
established connection. No behavior change with poll().

Add a unit test: with an urgent byte pending, waiting for RecvEvent
must not report ErrorEvent.

Co-authored-by: Cory Fields <cory-nospam-@coryfields.com>
Co-authored-by: Vasil Dimov <vd@FreeBSD.org>

caf5066e67 test: move send-stall wait into the framework

Move it out of p2p_ping_ibd.py and return the stalled byte count.

769169987d test: cover P2P TCP urgent data handling

Check that urgent indications do not prevent ordinary P2P input from
being processed or count as received message bytes.

Co-authored-by: Matthew Zipkin <pinheadmz@pm.me>

4e0089f9c9 test: cover P2P reset while sending

Reset a slow reader with block output stalled and more input queued
behind receive backpressure.

Add pack_linger() and the linux_host and windows_target checks
to the framework.

cb18aedce8 net: disconnect on poll errors before sending

Disconnect directly on POLLERR/POLLHUP when no read was requested,
skipping the send attempt that would otherwise fail and disconnect
the peer. This also changes the debug log message.

Co-authored-by: Cory Fields <cory-nospam-@coryfields.com>

ff2a39bb8f test: move wait_ignores_urgent_data next to the other wait test

It was placed above the socket pair tests to ease backporting.
Move-only, apart from the comment that said so.

00aad0e43b test: cover HTTP TCP urgent data and reset while sending

Check that an urgent byte does not disturb an ordinary request, and
reset a client while the server has unsent responses.

Co-authored-by: Matthew Zipkin <pinheadmz@pm.me>

ccd8095dfa http: handle socket errors separately from reads

When poll reports an error or hangup and no read was requested,
disconnect before sending instead of reading. This also changes the
debug log message.

Co-authored-by: Matthew Zipkin <pinheadmz@pm.me>
</commits>

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# Copyright (c) 2026 The Bitcoin Core developers
+# Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying
+# file COPYING or http://www.opensource.org/licenses/mit-license.php.
+"""Test P2P handling of TCP urgent data and resets while sending."""
+
+import socket
+
+from test_framework.messages import (
+    CInv,
+    MAGIC_BYTES,
+    MSG_BLOCK,
+    MSG_WITNESS_FLAG,
+    msg_getdata,
+    msg_ping,
+    msg_version,
+)
+from test_framework.netutil import pack_linger
+from test_framework.p2p import NetworkThread, P2PInterface, P2P_VERSION
+from test_framework.test_framework import BitcoinTestFramework
+from test_framework.util import assert_equal, assert_greater_than, mine_large_block, p2p_port
+from test_framework.wallet import MiniWallet
+
+
+def reset_on_close(sock):
+    """Make a subsequent close send a TCP reset and discard unsent data."""
+    sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_LINGER, pack_linger(enabled=True, timeout=0))
+
+
+class SocketErrorsTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
+    def set_test_params(self):
+        self.num_nodes = 1
+        self.extra_args = [["-maxsendbuffer=1", "-maxreceivebuffer=1"]]
+
+    def run_test(self):
+        self.message_builder = P2PInterface()
+        self.message_builder.magic_bytes = MAGIC_BYTES[self.chain]
+        self.version = msg_version()
+        self.version.nVersion = P2P_VERSION
+        self.check_urgent_bytes()
+        self.check_reset_while_sending()
+
+    def check_probe(self, send_probe, expected_bytes):
+        node = self.nodes[0]
+        with socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", p2p_port(0)), timeout=10) as peer:
+            self.wait_until(lambda: len(node.getpeerinfo()) == 1)
+            send_probe(peer)
+            # The node ignores the urgent byte: the connection stays open,
+            # the ordinary version message is processed and the urgent byte
+            # is not counted as received.
+            def received_version():
+                peers = node.getpeerinfo()
+                assert_equal(len(peers), 1)
+                return peers[0]["version"] == self.version.nVersion
+
+            self.wait_until(received_version)
+            assert_equal(node.getpeerinfo()[0]["bytesrecv"], expected_bytes)
+        self.wait_until(lambda: len(node.getpeerinfo()) == 0)
+
+    def check_urgent_bytes(self):
+        self.log.info("Check handling of individual urgent bytes")
+        version = self.message_builder.build_message(self.version)
+        # Use a fresh connection for each byte so earlier urgent indications
+        # cannot be overwritten before they are observed by the node.
+        for byte in b"URG":
+            def send_probe(peer):
+                peer.setsockopt(socket.IPPROTO_TCP, socket.TCP_NODELAY, 1)
+                assert_equal(peer.send(bytes([byte]), socket.MSG_OOB), 1)
+                peer.sendall(version)
+
